note: #944. Attachment.Address was the only address in Spec that reached a command unparsed, from the same restored Resource.Runtime as the network names of #909 and #932. At `ipv4.address=<it>` a dash cannot open a flag, but the value round-trips: restorePinnedAddress reads it back off the device, and Attach and that path both build `<it>/<len>` for the guest's `ip address add`, a bare argv element. The question is the third one of ownedAttachments, which Start, attachExtra and Attach all ask, so the cold and the hot plug share one rule. It is one condition, ParseAddr then Is4, because the zero Addr ParseAddr answers on failure is not Is4: a separate parse-error branch would be a term no mutation could redden, so there is none, and the two questions the table can tell apart are "is it IPv4" (every row) and "does it parse" (only the fe80 row passes it). Proven through the injectable runner, not against a running Incus. The same predicate is asked of Attachment.Secondary, which reaches the guest's `ip address add` through reconcileSecondary, and by restorePinnedAddress of the pin it reads back off the device: a device's config is state the host holds, so it is an untrusted input whoever wrote it, and a pin written before this lot comes back from there. The last two mutations hold the other end of the reconcile: guestAddresses reads what the guest says it carries, which the guest's root writes, and keeps only IPv4 addresses before reconcileSecondary and reconcileRoutedInterface turn them into `ip address del` arguments. The OVN re-plug repair reads two more values back off the device and is held the same way: repairGuestInterface asks ownedAttachments of the pin it puts back, and restoreExternalAddresses parses every entry of ipv4.routes.external as an IPv4 prefix before sending any. What the guest's `ip` would do with a crafted argument is not measured and not relied on: every check here refuses at the door, with a message naming the value. repairRoutedInterface reads three keys off a routed NIC, ipv4.address, ipv4.routes and ipv4.host_address, and parses all three before the first command; one mutation per key, each judged by the row that crafts that key alone.
